newsitem.title: CANADA: Bema says Chile gold lode may top 15 mln oz.
newsitem.headline: Bema says Chile gold lode may top 15 mln oz.

text.p: Bema Gold Corp said Friday that it believes its Cerro Casale deposit in Chile will ultimately prove to contain more than 15 million ounces of gold although more exploration work is needed.

"Fifteen million is actually a conservative estimate...I am very comfortable with the idea it will be in excess of 15 million with the potential to get much larger," Bema chief executive Clive Johnson said in an interview.
A company spokesman said some observers have speculated that the deposit could ultimately total more than 25 million ounces but Johnson declined to comment on those estimates.
He said Bema would likely issue further exploration results in about a month.
Johnson said investors appear to have misinterpreted data released Thursday from two drill holes. The news caused Bema's stock price to fall.

Investors appeared to focus primarily on lower gold grades from Hole 29, he said. The Bema spokesman said that hole was a probe intended to find the outer limit of the ore body. Johnson said it was not surprising then the grades were lower. More significant was that Hole 30 essentially doubled the width of the deposit to about 600 meters, the company said.
"I'm very puzzled by the market response. Not only are we optimistic but we are very pleased with the results," Johnson said.
Hole 30 "indicates we have the potential for a much larger deposit," he said. In addition, he said the deposit also remains open to the northeast.

The Bema spokesman said the company at Cerro Casale in the Andes has been drilling some of the deepest holes in South America, extending as far as 800 metres. An open-pit mine is envisaged. Company consultants believe mining and processing costs would be US$7.35 to US$8.35 a tonne.
Bema in the past has said it aims to develop the property itself despite rumors it could be a takeover target.
